root:
Print and copy TOTP/HOTP/Steam codes from an encrypted local vault.

  tess                     current codes for every account
  tess acme                one account's code, copied to the clipboard
  tess watch               live view with countdown bars
  tess add <uri|key|file>  add accounts
  tess vault init          create a vault

Usage:
  tess [query] [flags]
  tess [command]

Codes:
  code         Print the current code for a matching account (or all if omitted)
  verify       Check a code against an account
  watch        Live, auto-refreshing view with countdown bars and copy

Accounts:
  add          Add accounts from an otpauth/migration URI, a setup key, a QR image, an export file, the screen, or manual flags
  alias        Set an account's alias (the short name you type to reference it)
  dedupe       Move duplicate accounts to the Trash
  edit         Change an account's digits, period, algorithm, type, counter or secret
  list         List accounts (without codes)
  move         Move accounts into a folder (empty folder to clear)
  note         Set or clear an account's note
  order        Move an account to a position in every list
  pin          Pin accounts to the top of every list
  rename       Rename an account's issuer, account label, or alias
  restore      Bring accounts back from the Trash
  rm           Move accounts to the Trash
  show         Show an account's details (type, algorithm, digits, period, folder, tags)
  tag          Add or remove a tag on accounts
  trash        List the accounts in the Trash
  unpin        Unpin accounts

Transfer:
  export       Export accounts as otpauth URIs, base32 secrets, QR images, another app's export, or an encrypted vault copy
  import       Bulk-import accounts from files, other apps, Google exports, otpauth URIs, or QR images
  merge        Merge accounts from another Tessera vault or encrypted backup into this vault

Vault:
  vault        Manage the vault

Additional Commands:
  completion   Generate the autocompletion script for the specified shell
  help         Help about any command

Flags:
      --all[=true|false]       print the code of every account; never copies or advances a counter
      --at string              print the code at this time, RFC 3339 or unix seconds (time-based accounts; never copies)
      --clear int              clear the clipboard after this many seconds, 0 to keep (default $TESSERA_CLIP_CLEAR, else 30 on a terminal)
  -c, --copy[=true|false]      copy the code to the clipboard (the default on a terminal; -c copies even when piped)
  -h, --help[=true|false]      help for tess
      --json[=true|false]      output JSON (never copies)
      --next[=true|false]      for TOTP and Steam, the code of the following time step; for HOTP, advance and persist the counter
      --no-copy[=true|false]   print the code without touching the clipboard
      --now[=true|false]       print the current code instead of waiting for the next one
      --vault string           vault file path (default $TESSERA_VAULT or ~/.local/share/tessera/vault.json)
  -v, --version[=true|false]   version for tess

Use "tess [command] --help" for more information about a command.

commands.name: code
commands.help:
Print one account's code and copy it to the clipboard:

  tess code acme            # print and copy
  tess code acme --no-copy  # print only
  tess code acme --json     # machine-readable, never copies
  tess code --all           # every account's code; same as tess code
  tess code acme --at 2026-01-02T15:04:05Z
                            # the code at another time, never copies

The code is copied on a terminal. Piped or with --json, tess prints the raw
digits and leaves the clipboard alone unless you pass -c.

On a terminal, tess clears the copied code after 30 seconds if the clipboard
still holds it. --clear sets the delay; --clear 0 or TESSERA_CLIP_CLEAR=0
keeps the code.

Usage:
  tess code [query] [flags]

Flags:
      --all[=true|false]       print the code of every account; never copies or advances a counter
      --at string              print the code at this time, RFC 3339 or unix seconds (time-based accounts; never copies)
      --clear int              clear the clipboard after this many seconds, 0 to keep (default $TESSERA_CLIP_CLEAR, else 30 on a terminal)
  -c, --copy[=true|false]      copy the code to the clipboard (the default on a terminal; -c copies even when piped)
  -h, --help[=true|false]      help for code
      --json[=true|false]      output JSON (never copies)
      --next[=true|false]      for TOTP and Steam, the code of the following time step; for HOTP, advance and persist the counter
      --no-copy[=true|false]   print the code without touching the clipboard
      --now[=true|false]       print the current code instead of waiting for the next one

Global Flags:
      --vault string   vault file path (default $TESSERA_VAULT or ~/.local/share/tessera/vault.json)

commands.name: verify
commands.help:
Check whether a code belongs to an account. tess verify exits 0 when the
code is valid and 1 when it is not, and never copies.

For a time-based account the code may come from up to --window steps before
or after now. For an HOTP account it may come from the stored counter or the
--window counters after it; the counter is never changed.

Usage:
  tess verify <query> <code> [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for verify
      --window int          steps (or HOTP counters) away from now that still count as valid (default 1)

Global Flags:
      --vault string   vault file path (default $TESSERA_VAULT or ~/.local/share/tessera/vault.json)

commands.name: watch
commands.help:
Live, auto-refreshing view with countdown bars and copy

Usage:
  tess watch [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for watch
      --lock-after string   lock the view after this long without a key press, such as 5m, 0 to never lock (default $TESSERA_WATCH_LOCK, else 15m)

Global Flags:
      --vault string   vault file path (default $TESSERA_VAULT or ~/.local/share/tessera/vault.json)

commands.name: add
commands.help:
Add one or more accounts. The positional argument auto-detects:

  tess add "otpauth://totp/GitHub:me?secret=..."   # otpauth URI
  tess add ZB573K4APD63E6RLD3WAHI3QFZ35RLEP        # bare base32 setup key -> TOTP
  tess add code.png                                # QR image (all codes decoded)
  tess add export.json                             # Aegis/2FAS/Raivo export, or migration/otpauth lines
  tess add --screen                                # select a QR code on screen (macOS, Linux)
  cat export.json | tess add -                     # read the input from stdin
  tess add                                         # type the URI or setup key without echo
  tess add --secret - --issuer GitHub              # read the setup key from stdin

For a setup key, --issuer/--account/--digits/--period/--algorithm override the
TOTP defaults; --issuer also replaces the issuer of an otpauth URI. --qr and
--secret keep working as before.

Command-line arguments are visible to other processes and saved in shell
history. Run tess add with no argument to type a secret without echo, or pipe
it to tess add -.

Usage:
  tess add [input] [flags]

Flags:
      --account string        account name (manual/setup key)
      --algorithm string      SHA1|SHA256|SHA512 (manual/setup key) (default "SHA1")
      --digits int            code digits (manual/setup key) (default 6)
      --folder string         folder to place the account(s) in
  -h, --help[=true|false]     help for add
      --issuer string         issuer (manual, setup key, or otpauth URI)
      --period int            period seconds (manual/setup key) (default 30)
      --qr string             decode the account(s) from a QR image file (png/jpeg/webp/tiff/bmp)
      --screen[=true|false]   select a QR code on screen and add it (macOS, Linux)
      --secret string         base32 secret, or - to read it from stdin (manual)
      --type string           totp|hotp|steam (manual) (default "totp")

Global Flags:
      --vault string   vault file path (default $TESSERA_VAULT or ~/.local/share/tessera/vault.json)

commands.name: alias
commands.help:
Set an account's alias (the short name you type to reference it)

Usage:
  tess alias <account> <alias> [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for alias

Global Flags:
      --vault string   vault file path (default $TESSERA_VAULT or ~/.local/share/tessera/vault.json)

commands.name: dedupe
commands.help:
Find accounts with the same type, issuer, account and secret. The oldest of each
set stays; the others move to the Trash after you confirm.

Usage:
  tess dedupe [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for dedupe
  -y, --yes[=true|false]    skip the confirmation prompt

Global Flags:
      --vault string   vault file path (default $TESSERA_VAULT or ~/.local/share/tessera/vault.json)

commands.name: edit
commands.help:
Change the settings that make an account's codes.

  tess edit github --digits 8
  tess edit bank --type hotp --counter 12
  tess edit github --secret            # asks for the new secret
  pbpaste | tess edit github --secret  # reads it from stdin

Usage:
  tess edit <query> [flags]

Flags:
      --algorithm string      SHA1, SHA256 or SHA512
      --counter int           next counter value (hotp)
      --digits int            code digits, 6 to 8
  -h, --help[=true|false]     help for edit
      --period int            seconds each code lasts (totp, steam)
      --secret[=true|false]   replace the secret, read from a prompt or stdin
      --type string           totp, hotp or steam

Global Flags:
      --vault string   vault file path (default $TESSERA_VAULT or ~/.local/share/tessera/vault.json)

commands.name: list
commands.help:
List accounts (without codes)

Usage:
  tess list [flags]

Aliases:
  list, ls

Flags:
      --folder string       filter by folder
  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for list
      --json[=true|false]   output JSON
      --tag string          filter by tag

Global Flags:
      --vault string   vault file path (default $TESSERA_VAULT or ~/.local/share/tessera/vault.json)

commands.help:
Move accounts into a folder (empty folder to clear)

commands.name: note
commands.help:
Set the note on an account. tess show prints it; tess list does not.

  tess note github "recovery codes in the safe"
  pbpaste | tess note github -     # read the note from stdin
  tess note --clear github

Usage:
  tess note <query> [text] [flags]

Flags:
      --clear[=true|false]   remove the note
  -h, --help[=true|false]    help for note

Global Flags:
      --vault string   vault file path (default $TESSERA_VAULT or ~/.local/share/tessera/vault.json)

commands.name: order
commands.help:
Move an account to a position in every list, counting from 1. Pinned
accounts stay ahead of the others. --clear drops the account's position, so it
sorts by issuer and account again.

  tess order github 1
  tess order --clear github

Usage:
  tess order <query> <position> [flags]

Flags:
      --clear[=true|false]   drop the account's position
  -h, --help[=true|false]    help for order

Global Flags:
      --vault string   vault file path (default $TESSERA_VAULT or ~/.local/share/tessera/vault.json)

commands.name: pin
commands.help:
Pin accounts to the top of every list

Usage:
  tess pin <query>... [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for pin

Global Flags:
      --vault string   vault file path (default $TESSERA_VAULT or ~/.local/share/tessera/vault.json)

commands.help:
Rename an account's issuer, account label, or alias

Usage:
  tess rename <query> [flags]

Flags:
      --account string      new account label
      --alias string        new alias (the short name you type to reference the account)
  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for rename
      --issuer string       new issuer

Global Flags:
      --vault string   vault file path (default $TESSERA_VAULT or ~/.local/share/tessera/vault.json)

commands.name: restore
commands.help:
Bring accounts back from the Trash. Queries match trashed accounts only;
tess trash lists them. Every query must name exactly one account, or nothing
changes.

Usage:
  tess restore <query>... [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for restore

Global Flags:
      --vault string   vault file path (default $TESSERA_VAULT or ~/.local/share/tessera/vault.json)

commands.name: rm
commands.help:
Move accounts to the Trash. A trashed account gives no codes and is left out
of every list; tess restore brings it back.

--purge deletes the accounts and their secrets for good, from the Trash or
from the live accounts. It asks first; --yes skips the question and is
required when stdin is not a terminal.

Every query must name exactly one account, or nothing changes.

Usage:
  tess rm <query>... [flags]

Aliases:
  rm, remove, delete

Flags:
  -h, --help[=true|false]    help for rm
      --purge[=true|false]   delete for good instead of moving to the Trash
  -y, --yes[=true|false]     do not ask before deleting for good

Global Flags:
      --vault string   vault file path (default $TESSERA_VAULT or ~/.local/share/tessera/vault.json)

commands.name: show
commands.help:
Print one account's record. The secret is never shown unless you ask for it:

  tess show github            # details, no secret
  tess show github --secret   # also print the base32 setup key (cleartext)
  tess show github --uri      # also print the otpauth:// setup link (cleartext)
  tess show github --qr       # draw the setup link as a QR code to scan
  tess show github --json     # details as JSON, no secret

--qr refuses to write anywhere but a terminal unless you pass --force.

Usage:
  tess show <query> [flags]

Flags:
      --force[=true|false]    with --qr, write the QR code even when stdout is not a terminal
  -h, --help[=true|false]     help for show
      --json[=true|false]     output JSON (never includes the secret)
      --qr[=true|false]       draw the otpauth:// setup link as a QR code (holds the secret)
      --secret[=true|false]   also print the base32 setup key (cleartext)
      --uri[=true|false]      also print the otpauth:// setup link (cleartext)

Global Flags:
      --vault string   vault file path (default $TESSERA_VAULT or ~/.local/share/tessera/vault.json)

commands.name: tag
commands.help:
Add or remove a tag on accounts

Usage:
  tess tag <query>... <tag> [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help[=true|false]     help for tag
      --remove[=true|false]   remove the tag instead of adding it

Global Flags:
      --vault string   vault file path (default $TESSERA_VAULT or ~/.local/share/tessera/vault.json)

commands.name: trash
commands.help:
List the accounts in the Trash, most recently trashed first. Trashed
accounts give no codes and stay until tess restore brings them back or
tess trash empty deletes them for good.

Usage:
  tess trash [flags]
  tess trash [command]

Available Commands:
  empty       Delete the accounts in the Trash for good

Flags:
  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for trash
      --json[=true|false]   output JSON

Global Flags:
      --vault string   vault file path (default $TESSERA_VAULT or ~/.local/share/tessera/vault.json)

Use "tess trash [command] --help" for more information about a command.

subcommands.name: empty
subcommands.help:
Delete the accounts in the Trash and their secrets for good. --older-than
limits it to accounts trashed at least that long ago (30d, 12h). It asks
first; --yes skips the question and is required when stdin is not a
terminal.

Usage:
  tess trash empty [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for empty
      --older-than string   only accounts trashed at least this long ago, such as 30d or 12h
  -y, --yes[=true|false]    do not ask before deleting for good

Global Flags:
      --vault string   vault file path (default $TESSERA_VAULT or ~/.local/share/tessera/vault.json)

commands.name: unpin
commands.help:
Unpin accounts

Usage:
  tess unpin <query>... [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for unpin

Global Flags:
      --vault string   vault file path (default $TESSERA_VAULT or ~/.local/share/tessera/vault.json)

commands.name: export
commands.help:
Export account data (CLEARTEXT secrets — handle with care):

  tess export --uri                 # all accounts as otpauth:// URIs (bulk backup / migrate)
  tess export --uri github          # one account's otpauth URI
  tess export --secret github       # just the base32 secret (the raw key)
  tess export --qr ./qrcodes        # a QR PNG per account (scan into a phone)
  tess export --qr ./qrcodes github # one account's QR PNG
  tess export --file backup.json    # an encrypted copy of the whole vault (safe to store)
  tess export --format aegis        # the vault in another app's export format, on stdout
  tess export --format aegis --out aegis.json          # ... or written to a file
  tess export --format google-migration --out ./qr     # transfer QR codes for Google Authenticator

Trashed accounts are left out. Files are written readable by you only, and an
existing file is replaced only with --force.

Formats for --format:
  2fas              2FAS Auth backup JSON (no backup password)
  aegis             Aegis Authenticator vault JSON (unencrypted)
  andotp            andOTP plain backup JSON
  apple-csv         Apple Passwords CSV (Title,URL,...,OTPAuth)
  bitwarden         Bitwarden Authenticator JSON export
  google-migration  Google Authenticator transfer QR codes (PNG per batch)
  proton            Proton Authenticator JSON export (no password; TOTP and Steam only)

Usage:
  tess export [query] [flags]

Flags:
      --file string           write an encrypted copy of the vault to this path
      --force[=true|false]    replace files that already exist (--file, --qr and --out)
      --format string         rewrite the vault as another app's export: 2fas, aegis, andotp, apple-csv, bitwarden, google-migration, proton
  -h, --help[=true|false]     help for export
      --out string            where --format writes: a file, or a directory for multi-file formats (default stdout)
      --qr string             write a QR PNG per account to this directory (cleartext secrets)
      --secret[=true|false]   print only the base32 secret(s) (cleartext)
      --uri[=true|false]      print otpauth:// URIs (secrets in cleartext)

Global Flags:
      --vault string   vault file path (default $TESSERA_VAULT or ~/.local/share/tessera/vault.json)

commands.name: import
commands.help:
Import accounts in bulk. Sources combine and can be repeated; everything that
parses is imported, and items that fail are listed without aborting the batch:

  tess import accounts.txt export.json code.png   # paths auto-detect by content
  cat export.json | tess import -                 # read the input from stdin
  tess import --file accounts.txt                 # otpauth:// / otpauth-migration:// lines, or a setup key per line
  tess import --file export.json                  # an app export (see the list below)
  tess import --qr a.png --qr b.png               # QR images (multiple codes per image are all read)
  tess import --migration "otpauth-migration://offline?data=..."
  tess import --otpauth "otpauth://totp/...."

Exports it reads, recognized by content rather than by file name:

  Aegis, 2FAS, Raivo, andOTP, FreeOTP+, Stratum (Authenticator Pro),
  Bitwarden Authenticator, Bitwarden, Proton Authenticator, Ente Auth,
  Apple Passwords (CSV), 1Password (CSV and .1pux), and Google Authenticator
  (an otpauth-migration:// URI or a photo of its transfer QR code)

An export must be unencrypted; an encrypted one is refused by name rather than
half-read. Items with no one-time-password field, which is most of a password
manager's export, are left out. Duplicate accounts (same type, issuer, account
and secret) are skipped. docs/TRANSFER.md lists what to export from each app.

tess lists each account it added or skipped, each item it could not import
and why, then the totals. --json writes the same report as JSON.

Command-line arguments are visible to other processes and saved in shell
history. Run tess add with no argument to type a secret without echo, or pipe
it to tess add -.

Usage:
  tess import [path...] [flags]

Flags:
      --file stringArray        text, JSON, CSV or .1pux export file, - for stdin (repeatable)
  -h, --help[=true|false]       help for import
      --json[=true|false]       write the report as JSON
      --migration stringArray   Google Authenticator otpauth-migration:// URI (repeatable)
      --otpauth stringArray     single otpauth:// URI (repeatable)
      --qr stringArray          QR image file (repeatable; png/jpeg/webp/tiff/bmp)

Global Flags:
      --vault string   vault file path (default $TESSERA_VAULT or ~/.local/share/tessera/vault.json)

commands.name: merge
commands.help:
Merge another Tessera vault (or an encrypted backup exported from the macOS
app) into the current vault. Accounts are unioned, never dropped:

  - an account present in both (same id) keeps whichever copy was edited last
  - an account already present by content (same type/issuer/account/secret) is skipped
  - a copy that fails validation is left out
  - every other account is added

By default the source file is opened read-only and only the current vault is
written. --two-way applies the same rule in both directions and WRITES BOTH
FILES, so two vaults that have drifted apart end up holding the same accounts:

  tess merge --two-way ~/Library/.../app-vault.json

Each vault keeps its own handles. If the source shares this vault's passphrase
you are not prompted again; otherwise enter the source's passphrase (or set
$TESSERA_MERGE_PASSPHRASE).

Usage:
  tess merge <vault-file> [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help[=true|false]      help for merge
      --two-way[=true|false]   also write the missing and newer accounts back into the source vault

Global Flags:
      --vault string   vault file path (default $TESSERA_VAULT or ~/.local/share/tessera/vault.json)

commands.name: vault
commands.help:
Manage the vault

Usage:
  tess vault [command]

Available Commands:
  backup      Write today's backup file now
  forget      Remove the vault passphrase from the system secret store
  init        Create a new empty encrypted vault
  passwd      Change the vault passphrase
  rekey       Replace the vault key and keep the passphrase
  remember    Store the vault passphrase in the system secret store
  reset       Delete the vault file so a fresh vault can be created
  restore     Replace the vault with a backup
  status      Show the vault path, file details, and unlock methods

Flags:
  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for vault

Global Flags:
      --vault string   vault file path (default $TESSERA_VAULT or ~/.local/share/tessera/vault.json)

Use "tess vault [command] --help" for more information about a command.

subcommands.name: backup
subcommands.help:
Write the vault to tessera-backup-YYYYMMDD.json, named by the UTC date, in
$TESSERA_BACKUP_DIR or the folder given with --to. A backup written earlier the
same day is replaced. The file keeps only the passphrase unlock and opens with
the vault passphrase. The folder keeps the 30 newest backup files; older ones
are deleted, and no other file in it is touched.

With $TESSERA_BACKUP_DIR set, every change to the vault writes this file too.

Usage:
  tess vault backup [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for backup
      --to string           write to this folder instead of $TESSERA_BACKUP_DIR

Global Flags:
      --vault string   vault file path (default $TESSERA_VAULT or ~/.local/share/tessera/vault.json)

subcommands.name: forget
subcommands.help:
Remove the vault passphrase from the system secret store

Usage:
  tess vault forget [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for forget

Global Flags:
      --vault string   vault file path (default $TESSERA_VAULT or ~/.local/share/tessera/vault.json)

subcommands.name: init
subcommands.help:
Create a new empty encrypted vault

Usage:
  tess vault init [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for init

Global Flags:
      --vault string   vault file path (default $TESSERA_VAULT or ~/.local/share/tessera/vault.json)

subcommands.name: passwd
subcommands.help:
Change the vault passphrase. The current passphrase is read from
$TESSERA_PASSPHRASE or prompted for; the replacement is read from
$TESSERA_NEW_PASSPHRASE or entered twice on a terminal.

The vault key changes, so <vault>.bak and the files in $TESSERA_BACKUP_DIR,
which open with the old key, are deleted and today's backup is written under the
new one. An unlock method tess cannot re-create, such as the Touch ID unlock of
the Tessera app, is removed; the app adds it back the next time it is unlocked
with the passphrase.

A passphrase remembered in a system secret store is replaced with the new one.
The kernel keyring entry is removed instead; run "tess vault remember" to store
the new passphrase there.

Usage:
  tess vault passwd [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for passwd

Global Flags:
      --vault string   vault file path (default $TESSERA_VAULT or ~/.local/share/tessera/vault.json)

subcommands.name: rekey
subcommands.help:
Replace the key that encrypts the vault and keep the passphrase. The
passphrase is read from $TESSERA_PASSPHRASE or prompted for.

The vault key changes, so <vault>.bak and the files in $TESSERA_BACKUP_DIR,
which open with the old key, are deleted and today's backup is written under the
new one. An unlock method tess cannot re-create, such as the Touch ID unlock of
the Tessera app, is removed; the app adds it back the next time it is unlocked
with the passphrase.

Usage:
  tess vault rekey [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for rekey

Global Flags:
      --vault string   vault file path (default $TESSERA_VAULT or ~/.local/share/tessera/vault.json)

subcommands.name: remember
subcommands.help:
Store the vault passphrase in the system secret store so tess stops
prompting: the login keychain on macOS, the Secret Service on Linux with the
kernel keyring as a fallback, and Windows Credential Manager on Windows. The
passphrase is verified against the vault before it is stored.

The kernel keyring keeps the entry until reboot; --for sets an earlier expiry.

Usage:
  tess vault remember [flags]

Flags:
      --for duration        expire the stored passphrase after this long, such as 8h (kernel keyring only)
  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for remember

Global Flags:
      --vault string   vault file path (default $TESSERA_VAULT or ~/.local/share/tessera/vault.json)

subcommands.name: reset
subcommands.help:
Delete the vault at its resolved path (respects --vault and $TESSERA_VAULT).
This is irreversible and removes every account. Run "tess vault init" afterward
to create a new empty vault. Use --force to skip the confirmation in scripts.

Usage:
  tess vault reset [flags]

Flags:
      --force[=true|false]   skip the confirmation prompt
  -h, --help[=true|false]    help for reset

Global Flags:
      --vault string   vault file path (default $TESSERA_VAULT or ~/.local/share/tessera/vault.json)

subcommands.name: restore
subcommands.help:
Replace the vault with a backup: <vault>.bak with --bak, or a file such as
one from $TESSERA_BACKUP_DIR. The file must open with its passphrase, read from
$TESSERA_PASSPHRASE, the system secret store, or a prompt. The vault it replaces
becomes <vault>.bak. tess asks before replacing a vault; --yes skips the question.

Usage:
  tess vault restore [file | --bak] [flags]

Flags:
      --bak[=true|false]    restore <vault>.bak, the vault as it was before the last write
  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for restore
  -y, --yes[=true|false]    replace the vault without asking

Global Flags:
      --vault string   vault file path (default $TESSERA_VAULT or ~/.local/share/tessera/vault.json)

subcommands.name: status
subcommands.help:
Report the resolved vault path, whether the file exists, its size and
modification time, the format version, the unlock methods in the envelope
header and the argon2id cost of each passphrase unlock, whether <vault>.bak
exists, the $TESSERA_BACKUP_DIR folder and the date of its newest backup, and
which system secret store holds the passphrase. Nothing is decrypted and the
passphrase is never shown.

Usage:
  tess vault status [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for status
      --json[=true|false]   output JSON

Global Flags:
      --vault string   vault file path (default $TESSERA_VAULT or ~/.local/share/tessera/vault.json)

commands.name: completion
commands.help:
Generate the autocompletion script for tess for the specified shell.
See each sub-command's help for details on how to use the generated script.

Usage:
  tess completion [command]

Available Commands:
  bash        Generate the autocompletion script for bash
  fish        Generate the autocompletion script for fish
  powershell  Generate the autocompletion script for powershell
  zsh         Generate the autocompletion script for zsh

Flags:
  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for completion

Global Flags:
      --vault string   vault file path (default $TESSERA_VAULT or ~/.local/share/tessera/vault.json)

Use "tess completion [command] --help" for more information about a command.

subcommands.name: bash
subcommands.help:
Generate the autocompletion script for the bash shell.

This script depends on the 'bash-completion' package.
If it is not installed already, you can install it via your OS's package manager.

To load completions in your current shell session:

	source <(tess completion bash)

To load completions for every new session, execute once:

#### Linux:

	tess completion bash > /etc/bash_completion.d/tess

#### macOS:

	tess completion bash > $(brew --prefix)/etc/bash_completion.d/tess

You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.

Usage:
  tess completion bash

Flags:
  -h, --help[=true|false]              help for bash
      --no-descriptions[=true|false]   disable completion descriptions

Global Flags:
      --vault string   vault file path (default $TESSERA_VAULT or ~/.local/share/tessera/vault.json)

subcommands.name: fish
subcommands.help:
Generate the autocompletion script for the fish shell.

To load completions in your current shell session:

	tess completion fish | source

To load completions for every new session, execute once:

	tess completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/tess.fish

You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.

Usage:
  tess completion fish [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help[=true|false]              help for fish
      --no-descriptions[=true|false]   disable completion descriptions

Global Flags:
      --vault string   vault file path (default $TESSERA_VAULT or ~/.local/share/tessera/vault.json)

subcommands.name: powershell
subcommands.help:
Generate the autocompletion script for powershell.

To load completions in your current shell session:

	tess completion powershell | Out-String | Invoke-Expression

To load completions for every new session, add the output of the above command
to your powershell profile.

Usage:
  tess completion powershell [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help[=true|false]              help for powershell
      --no-descriptions[=true|false]   disable completion descriptions

Global Flags:
      --vault string   vault file path (default $TESSERA_VAULT or ~/.local/share/tessera/vault.json)

subcommands.name: zsh
subcommands.help:
Generate the autocompletion script for the zsh shell.

If shell completion is not already enabled in your environment you will need
to enable it.  You can execute the following once:

	echo "autoload -U compinit; compinit" >> ~/.zshrc

To load completions in your current shell session:

	source <(tess completion zsh)

To load completions for every new session, execute once:

#### Linux:

	tess completion zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_tess"

#### macOS:

	tess completion zsh > $(brew --prefix)/share/zsh/site-functions/_tess

You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.

Usage:
  tess completion zsh [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help[=true|false]              help for zsh
      --no-descriptions[=true|false]   disable completion descriptions

Global Flags:
      --vault string   vault file path (default $TESSERA_VAULT or ~/.local/share/tessera/vault.json)
